known.title: Load agent accounts beyond the first members page
Ignore key responses from earlier dialog openings
Handle offline agent mutations instead of leaving them pending
Gate: adding an agent with the Admin role
Later: TOOLS and TOOLSPY must complete the feature-tool contract

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - an organisation with 100 existing members adds its first agent. This filters only the members already fetched by useMembers, whose request is fixed to page=1&limit=100 (members-hooks.ts:14). Both APIs sort oldest first; the TypeScript implementation is organisations.service.ts:177. The newly added agent therefore never appears, leaving the admin unable to create or revoke its key through the screen. Fetch subsequent pages or provide an independently paginated agent list.
findings.title: Load agent accounts beyond the first members page

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - on a slow connection, an admin closes the Creating key dialog and reopens it to try again. Every invocation unconditionally calls setKey when its promise resolves. If the first response is delayed until after the second key is created and displayed, it overwrites the field with the first, now-revoked key. Closing also cannot clear a response that arrives afterward. Associate results with the current opening and discard results from closed or superseded openings.
findings.title: Ignore key responses from earlier dialog openings

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - an admin loses connectivity while the Members screen is open, then clicks Create key. These mutations use the default online network mode, which [pauses mutations while offline](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/network-mode). query-client.ts:6 sets networkMode='always' only for queries. The dialog consequently stays on Creating key without a connection message or retry action. The new add-agent and revoke-key hooks and AgentAccessDialog's mutation have the same fault; the switch can display an unsaved change throughout the outage. Handle paused mutations explicitly or make these online-only operations fail promptly with their existing recovery messages.
findings.title: Handle offline agent mutations instead of leaving them pending

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - an admin chooses Admin when adding an agent. The browser flow checks the default Member selection and submits without changing it or asserting the resulting role. Both APIs' success/history cases likewise assert only Member; their other Admin-agent setups never assert the returned role. A form that always submits Member, or either service silently assigning Member, passes all these proofs despite violating item 2's explicit Admin-or-Member choice. Exercise selecting Admin through the browser and verify the saved role, while retaining the existing Member checks.
findings.title: Gate: adding an agent with the Admin role

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 5, Harm 2
The test named test_3_each_feature_has_its_tools currently verifies dialog generation and browser flows only. Neither starter contains the tool engine or feature tools, and there is no older-starter parameter or fallback verification. Item 3's tool schemas, annotations, agent permissions/history, generated tools and hide/add behavior therefore remain unproved and unimplemented. These are explicitly assigned to TOOLS and TOOLSPY, so this is deferred advice rather than a blocking Not done finding against AGENTS.
findings.title: Later: TOOLS and TOOLSPY must complete the feature-tool contract
